::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
📄 **For the group work:** [download this grid as a PDF](s_08a_ConflictAnalysis.pdf). The
lecture slides explain where each question comes from, with lithium mining in the Salar de Atacama, Chile, as a worked example.
:::
:::

**Task (20 min, country groups).** Open the [Environmental Justice Atlas](https://ejatlas.org)
and filter by your country. Pick **one** conflict — ideally one linked to a major export of
your country. If there is no case for your country, take one linked to its main export commodity
(Atlas of Economic Complexity). Work through the seven questions. Report in **2 minutes, starting with question 7**.

**Why these questions.** The grid draws on two works. Its structure follows the conceptual
framework of @scheidel2018: conflicts over the environment arise from a growing social
metabolism (the *metabolic driver*), are carried by particular *actors*, are fought in
different *valuation languages*, and unfold in stages of *mobilisation* (questions 2, 3, 5
and 6). The guiding questions follow the template on which every EJAtlas case is coded
[@temper2015], so most answers can be found on the case page.

**The column "Based on"** names, for each question, the work its concepts come from. That is
where to read further, and what to cite on your poster. Besides the two works above, these
are Martínez-Alier's work on valuation languages [@martinezalier2002; @martinezalier2010],
the global analyses of EJAtlas cases on impacts [@scheidel2023] and on mobilisation, outcomes
and violence [@scheidel2020; @navas2018], and, for question 7, your trade analysis from
Session 5 and the net resource flows measured by @dorninger2021 (Session 6).

| | Topic | Guiding questions | Based on |
|:-:|:-----------------|:---------------------------------------------|:---------------|
| **1** | **Project and place** | Which project, which commodity, which type of conflict? Where exactly, since when? | @temper2015 |
| **2** | **Metabolic driver** | Which flow of materials, energy, water or waste is at stake? Where does the commodity go — who consumes it? Who receives the benefits, who bears the costs? | @scheidel2018; @martinezalier2010 |
| **3** | **Actors** | Companies (and their home countries), state agencies, financiers; affected and mobilising groups, NGOs. Who has power, money, legal standing? | @scheidel2018; @temper2015 |
| **4** | **Impacts** | Environmental, health and socio-economic impacts. Visible already, or potential? Which groups are hit hardest? | @temper2015; @scheidel2023 |
| **5** | **Valuation languages** | In which terms do the parties argue — money, jobs, compensation, or livelihood, territory, sacredness, rights? Are some languages excluded from the decision? | @martinezalier2002; @martinezalier2010 |
| **6** | **Mobilisation and outcome** | Preventive, reacting to the project, or demanding reparation? Forms of protest, litigation, intensity. Repression or violence — direct, but also slow or structural? Outcome? | @scheidel2020; @navas2018 |
| **7** | **So what?** For your poster | What does the case tell you about your country's position in world trade — and about the twin challenge of social provisioning and ecological sustainability? | Session 5; @dorninger2021 |

**Read the atlas critically.** The EJAtlas lists conflicts that were *documented*, often
together with those mobilising [@temper2015]. Coverage differs strongly between countries
[@scheidel2023], and a missing entry does not mean there is no conflict. Treat a case page
as a starting point: check it against at least one peer-reviewed case study or another
independent source, and note on your poster where your information comes from.

**Background.** Why the poor often defend the environment — because they live from it — is
the subject of the *environmentalism of the poor* [@martinezalier2002;
@anguelovski2014]. A global overview of what mobilisations achieve and at what risk is
@scheidel2020. The worked example in the lecture draws on @floresfernandez2023 and @jerez2021.
